question: Walking at (5)/(6) of his normal speed from his home, Tarun is 16 minutes late in reaching his office. The usual time taken by him to cover the distance between his home and his office is:
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Speed = 5/6 → Time = 6/5 (inverse)

Increase in time = (6/5 − 1) = 1/5 of usual time

Given increase = 16 minutes

So (1/5) time = 16 → time = 80 minutes

**∴ Answer = 80 minutes**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Reduced speed = (5/6) of normal speed, delay = 16 minutes

**Formula used:**

Time = Distance ÷ Speed

**Calculation:**

⇒ Let usual time = t minutes

⇒ New time = (6/5)t

⇒ Increase = (6/5)t − t = (1/5)t

⇒ (1/5)t = 16

⇒ t = 80

**∴ The usual time is 80 minutes.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Inverse Relation

Speed and time are inversely proportional.

Speed Reduction

If speed = a/b, time = b/a

Time Difference

Extra time = new − original

Shortcut Insight

Use fractional increase directly.
